commits.message:
[Fix][RawBlock] Cap uring_cmd auto transfer size by max_segments (#3882)

[Bugfix] raw_block: cap auto max_data_transfer_size by NVMe max_segments

With use_uring_cmd=true, _resolve_max_data_transfer_size auto-detected the I/O split size from max_hw_sectors_kb only, ignoring the device's max_segments scatter-gather limit. The NVMe io_uring_cmd passthrough builds one iovec segment per page, so a transfer larger than max_segments*page_size is rejected by the kernel with EINVAL and every large store/load fails.

Cap the auto-detected size at min(max_hw_sectors_kb*1024, max_segments*page_size), falling back to the max_hw_sectors_kb value when max_segments sysfs is absent.

commits.author: Cao Qian
commits.message:
[Operator] Remove Hardcoded CacheBlend webhook-injected vLLM params (#4424)

* [Operator] Make CacheBlend webhook-injected vLLM params configurable

The mutating webhook hardcoded --block-size 64 and --attention-backend
CUSTOM, silently overwriting user-supplied values, and offered no way to
set env vars on the vLLM container or extra cb.* connector config. That
blocks models that deviate from the baseline profile: sparse-attention
models needing --block-size 128, all-sparse-MLA models whose arch
adapter must NOT get --attention-backend, fp8-MoE models needing
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP8=0, and models needing extra cb.* knobs.

Add four CacheBlendEngine spec fields, all defaulting to the previous
hardcoded behavior:

- injection.blockSize (default 64): injected --block-size value.
- injection.attentionBackend (default CUSTOM): injected
  --attention-backend; the sentinel "none" omits the flag and leaves a
  user-supplied value untouched.
- injection.env: extra env vars set on the target vLLM container
  (same-name vars overwritten; PYTHONPATH rejected by validation and
  skipped by the builder - the plugin staging owns it).
- blend.extraConfig (map[string]JSON): extra kv_connector_extra_config
  entries merged last into the connection ConfigMap, able to override
  auto-generated keys (mirroring extraArgs semantics).

Signed-off-by: aeon-x <talexcao@gmail.com>

* [Operator] Replace blend.extraConfig with typed blend.partialBucket

Review feedback: a free-form JSON map is more surface than the one knob
that needs it. cb.partial_bucket is the only extra connector key a
known model profile requires (fp8-MoE PARTIAL row padding, keeping the
Triton autotuner from re-tuning per CB step), so expose it as a typed,
validated field instead. Unset omits the key (padding disabled);
validation requires >= 1 when set.

commits.author: Jinhwan Suk (석진환)
commits.message:
[Platform][RBLN] Add RBLN device backend for engine-driven MP transfer (#4450)

* [Platform][RBLN] Add RBLN device backend for engine-driven MP transfer

Adds Rebellions NPUs as a device-registry entry. `torch.rbln` comes from
torch-rbln through a torch backend entry point, so it is visible on a bare
`import torch`; the engine is vllm-rbln. Without a registry entry,
detection falls back to the CPU stub and no RBLN path works at all.

Scope is multiprocess engine-driven transfer, which is self-contained: the
MP path builds no GPU connector, resolving layouts through
`normalize_kv_and_discover_format` and moving KV through `RblnDeviceOps`.
The in-process connector follows separately.

LMCache-driven MP is refused up front. `torch.rbln` exposes device
discovery, `set_device()` and `synchronize()` but no `Stream` / `Event`,
and that path orders its cross-process handoff with an event, so
`RblnDeviceSpec` reports `is_handle_transfer_available()` as False and
leaves `ipc_wrapper_cls` / `event_ipc_backend` at their None defaults --
`mp_transfer_mode=lmcache_driven` then fails at its documented validation
point instead of on an attribute lookup later.

The per-layer KV cache is 6-D: vllm-rbln allocates
`[2, NB, NH, 1, BS, HS]`, HND with an extra axis between heads and block
tokens that the RBLN attention backend requires. Axis 3 is always 1, so the
bytes and strides are those of NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS one axis short.

It is registered as its own EngineKVFormat.NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS (15)
rather than squeezed into format 6 during discovery. Reshaping inside
detection would need a device hook, making discovery depend on
process-global device state instead of being a pure function of
`(kv_caches, layout_hints)`, and would force a second device-specific rule
for a layout that is HND by definition. As its own format, the 6-D branch
in `detectors/vllm.py` keys off the shape signature alone (rank 6, leading
axis 2, axis 3 == 1), so the same input classifies identically on any host,
the detector needs no `rbln` entry in its HND table, and the reported
layout -- which vllm-rbln never sets, leaving `get_kv_cache_layout()` at
its NHD default -- plays no part.

Squeezing the axis in `attempt_permute_to_contiguous_view` was also
rejected: a blanket singleton squeeze silently misclassifies vLLM HND with
`num_kv_heads == 1` (any TP size equal to the KV-head count) as a rank-4
blocks-first fused format, and breaks SGLang MLA outright, whose detection
keys off `shape[1] == 1`.

No transfer kernel handles format 15. RBLN has no compiled block-transfer
extension in tree, and the CUDA / SYCL kernels never see an RBLN cache, so
their `default:` arm rejecting it is correct rather than a gap. csrc
carries only the enum value and its `FORMAT_FACTS` row; `ops_types.py`
mirrors the value, which `test_c_ops_parity` requires to match exactly.

`RblnDeviceOps` inherits the torch baseline for every op except
`multi_layer_block_kv_transfer`, which stages each chunk head-major
(`[2, L, H, T, D]`) rather than upstream's token-major `[2, L, T, H*D]`.
Filling a token-major chunk from an HND paged buffer costs an on-device
head/token permute per store and restore; head-major issues none. The
chunk keeps the byte size upstream sized it to and is reinterpreted with a
free view. Sound because the engine-driven pair writes and reads it with
the same code and the cache server treats it as an opaque byte range. It
applies `squeeze_singleton_axis` at entry, so `kv_ops.py` indexes a 5-D
tensor and the singleton stays out of every axis offset below.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Platform][RBLN] Drop the unused is_native_kv_structure predicate

The predicate was the tolerant guard for a `normalize_kv_caches` hook on
`DeviceSpec`: format discovery handed the hook every KV structure it saw,
so the RBLN override had to recognize a flat list of native 6-D tensors
and pass everything else through untouched.

That design is gone. The native layout is now its own
`EngineKVFormat.NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS`, detection reshapes nothing,
and the squeeze moved down into `RblnDeviceOps`, which knows from the
detected format what it holds and uses the strict
`squeeze_singleton_axis`. Nothing under `lmcache/` calls the predicate
any more -- only its own test did -- so remove it along with the
`DiscoverableKVCache` import it needed and the design-doc mention.

`is_rbln_kv_layout` stays: `squeeze_singleton_axis` is built on it.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Platform][RBLN] Stage chunks in the canonical token-major wire layout

RblnDeviceOps staged each chunk head-major ([2, L, H, T, D]) to avoid the
head<->token transpose that filling a token-major chunk from an HND cache
requires. That made an RBLN chunk unreadable by any other device, which
is the whole point of a wire layout, and it is not necessary: the
transpose can run on the host instead of inside the device<->host copy.

Chunks are now staged in LMCache's canonical [2, L, T, H*D]. Gather reads
each block's K and V straight out of the paged cache into a host buffer
laid out [B, L, 2, H, BS, D] -- both sides contiguous, no device-side
gather and no device buffer -- and transposes into the chunk on the host.
Scatter mirrors it. K and V are addressed separately because
layer[:, block] spans both halves of a layer and is not contiguous.

Measured on Qwen3-1.7B (28L, 8 heads, head_size 128, bf16, block 1024,
one block per chunk):

  gather  D2H   19.5 GB/s   (head-major staging reached 3.8 GB/s here)
  scatter H2D   19.2 GB/s   (head-major staging reached 24.5 GB/s)

so the canonical layout costs nothing on the store path and stays within
reach on the restore path. Block ids being scattered rather than
contiguous makes no difference: no copy spans a block boundary either
way.

test_chunk_matches_the_canonical_torch_path pins the output byte-for-byte
against the shared torch path. The staging buffers are thread-local: the
multiprocess server runs blocking handlers on a thread pool, so a store
and a retrieve can be in multi_layer_block_kv_transfer at once, and
sharing one buffer corrupted the KV cache with no error raised.
test_staging_concurrency covers that and fails on a shared buffer.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

mirror its bounce logic in batched_read. Add 4 env-guarded tests verifying
unaligned read/batched_read, short-buffer bounce, and per-item decisions.

commits.author: Samuel Shen
commits.message:
[Refactor]: vLLM LBHNC KVLayout metadata (#4729)

* [Fix] Restore vLLM KV cache layout discovery after vllm#51718

vllm#51718 (RFC vllm#42082) moved layout resolution onto
CacheConfig.kv_cache_layout and removed
vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils.get_kv_cache_layout, so the kv_layout
registration hint silently vanished on vLLM nightlies.

Read the resolved layout from CacheConfig (falling back to the legacy
backend query on older vLLM), normalize standardized KVCacheLayout
names onto the existing NHD/HND vocabulary, and raise at registration
for the four layouts LMCache cannot transfer yet instead of
misclassifying them as NHD.

Part of #3560.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Clarify unsupported-layout remediation: backend-required layouts cannot be overridden via env

Found in E2E: DeepSeek V4's attention backend requires BLHNC, so the
previous suggestion to set VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT was not actionable there
(backend-required outranks the env var in vLLM's resolution order).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* [Fix] Express LMCache's preferred KV cache layout to vLLM

Non-MLA models prefer the standardized head-contiguous layout (LBHNC);
MLA defers since layout is immaterial for a single latent head, and
pre-standardization vLLM gets the legacy HND name. The standardized
name is returned rather than its alias because MultiConnector compares
preference strings verbatim. Backend-required layouts and
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT still outrank a preference and remain validated
at registration.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Keep LayoutHints.kv_layout strictly NHD/HND; translate at the vLLM boundary

Review feedback: kv_layout exists only to disambiguate the heads/tokens
order that shape sniffing cannot; engine formats live in EngineKVFormat.
Move the standardized-name translation (and the unsupported-layout
fail-loud) from kv_format/types.py into integration/vllm/utils.py, and
have the detector reject hints outside the two-value contract instead
of importing a vLLM vocabulary.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Fail loud when layout hints are built before resolution

Registration always runs after vLLM resolves the layout, so an
unresolved CacheConfig here means a caller bug (hints built at
construction time, or an ambient default config); raise with the
precondition instead of silently skipping the hint. The MP worker
adapter captures hints once per process -- the layout is final for the
process lifetime and heartbeat recovery may re-register from a context
without the ambient vLLM config.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Support the blocks-first standardized layouts (BLHNC/BLNHC)

The kv_layout hint now carries the standardized layout vocabulary
(legacy NHD/HND spellings canonicalize at the vLLM boundary), and the
vLLM detector goes declaration-first: a blocks-first hint makes it
verify that the registered per-layer views share one storage with the
declared strides -- any drift raises -- and reconstruct the single
cross-layer tensor.

Two EngineKVFormat members join their NB_NL_TWO_* siblings with K/V
packed in the content dim: NB_NL_NH_BS_CS (BLHNC) and NB_NL_BS_NH_CS
(BLNHC). Their specs hand the kernels per-layer base pointers one
(layer, block) chunk apart, and page_buffer_offset gains the inflated
per-block step (num_layers * chunk) that blocks-first addressing
needs. GPU round-trip tests pin the kernels against a pure-torch
reference in both directions.

LHBNC and BHLNC remain rejected: their per-(layer, block) content is
fragmented per head, which PageBufferShapeDesc cannot describe.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Blocks-first transfers through HMA-shared pools

DeepSeek V4's pool interleaves groups with different geometry, so a
group's per-block step exceeds num_layers * chunk. Reconstruction now
accepts (and preserves) the observed step, the connector reads it off
the reconstructed tensor, and multi_layer_kv_transfer carries it to
the kernels as block_stride_elems (0 = tight). Pointer initialization
goes through spec.data_ptrs so cross-layer formats hand the kernels
per-layer bases. GPU round-trip tests cover tight and padded pools.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Reconstruct blocks-first groups interleaved inside HMA blocks

DeepSeek V4 pools weave groups within each block, so one group's
consecutive layers sit a uniform step apart that exceeds its own
chunk. Observe and verify the step (uniform spacing, block step large
enough to hold all layers), carry it as the reconstructed tensor's
layer stride, and let the per-layer base pointers absorb it in the
kernels.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Carry canonical layout names and reconstructed tensors through the MP group path

Found by MP-mode E2E: the subpaged-MLA group edit still enforced the
legacy two-name kv_layout contract and rejected canonical names, and
per-group discovery integer-indexed the reconstructed cross-layer
tensor as if it were a per-layer list. Group edits now accept the
canonical spellings, and cross-layer sub-groups keep their single
reconstructed tensor (identity grouping folds the repeats).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Identity grouping reads geometry off the reconstructed cross-layer tensor

Cross-layer entries in the normalized per-layer list are the whole
reconstructed tensor, not per-layer slices; indexing the outer list by
layer fed a list into the spec accessors.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Group representatives resolve their spec source through one helper

Third occurrence of the same slip (engine discovery, identity grouping,
now the layer-groups manager): a cross-layer group's representative
entry is the reconstructed whole-group tensor and must not be wrapped
as a per-layer list. group_spec_source() owns the choice.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Route every group-representative spec access through group_spec_source

The layer-groups manager's block-stride probe and shape-desc builder
still passed the outer per-layer list for cross-layer groups.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Group data pointers resolve cross-layer groups locally

get_group_data_ptrs passed the outer per-layer list and global layer
indices; a cross-layer group's spec needs its reconstructed tensor and
group-local indices. Adds a DSV4-shaped construction test: two groups
with different geometry interleaved in one blocks-first pool, through
normalize -> manager -> group pointers.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* MP block-transfer kernels address the blocks-first formats

Per-layer base pointers land one (layer, block) chunk apart and
scalars_per_block() already carries the interleaved step through
block_stride_elems, so the new formats reuse the per-layer address
shape; NB_NL_NH_BS_CS joins the HND within-block branch.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Apply isort and clang-format across the branch

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Import the MP connector lazily in the preference tests

Importing lmcache_mp_connector at collection time initializes
process-wide MP transfer state, which the cache-server tests later
trip over when the whole suite runs in one process. The isolation
defect predates this branch; importing inside a fixture keeps the
preference tests out of that ordering.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Note why the heads-outermost layouts stay unsupported

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Mark the heads-outermost layout gap as TODO

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Treat layout hints as registration payload, not adapter-computed state

The connector already builds the hints for group edits; forward them
through register_kv_caches and persist them beside kv_caches and
engine_group_infos for heartbeat re-registration, instead of the
adapter lazily computing its own copy from the ambient config.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Scope the CPU-backend HND override to layer-compact hints

The override works around vLLM's CPU attention backend misreporting
the layer-compact layout; it was also stomping explicit blocks-first
declarations, which broke reconstruction everywhere torch runs on CPU
(the ubuntu CI matrix).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Match the torch fallback's multi_layer_kv_transfer signature to cuda_ops

The CUDA binding gained block_stride_elems; the fallback mirrors it
and rejects the blocks-first cross-layer formats it does not
implement, following the file's existing HND precedent. Caught by
test_function_signature_parity on k3.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Resolve cross-layer entries inside the spec accessors

Review feedback: the geometry accessors own the mapping from a
normalized per-layer structure onto what a format's spec expects, so
call sites stay uniform. One documented resolver replaces the
per-call-site source juggling and the group_spec_source helper, and
bare cross-layer tensors pass through unchanged again.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Own the kv_layout vocabulary in kv_format.types

The canonical-spelling map was declared in the vLLM detector and
re-spelled inline in the group edits; the vocabulary module that
defines KVLayoutName owns it now and both consume it.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Skip the connector preference tests where vLLM is not installed

The k3 unit environment installs LMCache without vLLM; the lazy
connector import now skips there instead of erroring.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Split the data_ptrs docstring into one paragraph per pointer shape

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Resolve block_stride_elems through the layout getter

Both connector classes computed it inline from is_cross_layer checks;
route them through resolve_block_stride_and_log_layout and give the
torch fallback an _is_blocks_first_format predicate beside its
existing _is_*_format helpers.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Trim comments to load-bearing facts

Also fix the NB_NL_BS_NH_CS module docstring (the [BS, NH, CS] order
is NHD, not HND) and move the enum doc comments for 17/18 in front of
their members like the rest of the file.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop layout-name canonicalization; keep NHD and HND

translate_vllm_kv_cache_layout now maps vLLM's LBNHC/LBHNC to NHD/HND
at the boundary, so hints and detection keep the names LMCache has
always used, plus BLHNC/BLNHC which have no legacy spelling. Deletes
CANONICAL_KV_LAYOUTS. get_required_kvcache_layout still returns
LBHNC because that string goes to vLLM.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Leave kv_cache_group_edits.py untouched

With hints carrying NHD/HND again the file needs no change; restore
it to dev byte for byte.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop drive-by edits to unrelated files

Restore two READMEs, the cache-simulator README, and
record_strategies/base.py, which a repo-wide format pass had
reformatted; none are touched by this change. Keep the dev wording of
the kv_layout hint doc, appending only the new names.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Keep get_num_blocks at two arguments

The cross-layer unwrap lives inside the getter, so dev's call site
works unchanged for every group and kv_layer_groups.py returns to dev
byte for byte.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Name the fallback guard for what it tests

Blocks-outermost is not the same as cross-layer: TRT-LLM's
NB_NL_TWO_NH_BS_HS is cross-layer without fused KV and the NL_X_*_CS
formats are fused without being cross-layer; the fallback supports
both. The guard rejects exactly the cross-layer fused pair, so call
it that.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Derive every layout-name check from KVLayoutName

KVLayoutName is the one place the accepted vocabulary is written;

commits.author: Hoang Minh An
commits.message:
fix(mp): don't let one bad frame kill the shared client polling loop (#4765)

* fix(mp): don't let one bad frame kill the shared client polling loop

`ClientPollingLoop` runs a single process-wide daemon thread that services
every `MessageQueueClient`, and `_main_loop` calls `owner.process_inbound()`
without a guard. `process_inbound` decodes peer-supplied bytes in four places,
so any decode failure propagates out of the loop and terminates the thread.
Nothing supervises or restarts it, so every client in the process is stranded:
pending futures never resolve and new requests only ever time out, until the
process is restarted. The traceback goes to the dying thread's stderr, so
nothing actionable surfaces to the application.

This is reachable today between adjacent releases. `RequestType` is an
`enum.auto()` enum, so a member's wire value is its declaration position, and
the list is not append-only: between v0.5.2 (36 members) and v0.5.4 (40) three
members were inserted at positions 3-5, shifting 34 existing values (STORE 3->6,
RETRIEVE 4->7, PING 19->22) and extending the range. A peer on the newer
protocol therefore answers with values an older peer cannot decode. Since the
cache-server and engine-side images are versioned independently, a mismatched
pair is an ordinary deployment state.

Wrap the dispatch so an undecodable or otherwise unexpected frame is logged and
dropped while the loop keeps serving. The offending request still times out --
without a usable request_type it cannot be matched to its future -- but the
blast radius is now that one request instead of the whole process.

The regression test asserts the observable contract through the public API
only: after a response the client cannot decode, a later well-formed request
must still complete. Without the guard that second request times out too.

Signed-off-by: anhm5 <anhm5@fpt.com>

* fix(mp): annotate the futures in the new polling-loop test for mypy

The new test carries a `-> None` annotation, so unlike its neighbours mypy
checks its body. `submit_request` returns `MessagingFuture[T]` and the call
does not pass `response_cls`, leaving `T` unbound, so mypy asks for an explicit
annotation on both locals. `GET_CHUNK_SIZE` responds with `int`.

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Fix][CB] Decide fused-KV packing per group, not per registration (#4850)

`_cb_group_rope_geometry` read `is_fused_packed` from the group's
`engine_kv_format`, but that format is detected once per REGISTRATION while
fused-ness is a per-GROUP property.

MiniMax-M3 registers a fused `2 * head_size` main K/V group (60 layers)
alongside a key-only `head_size` lightning-indexer side cache (57 layers).
Both are rank 4 -- the fused signature -- and both report `kv_size == 1`, so
the shared format labelled the index group fused too. `per_head` became
`2 * head_size`, which does not divide that group's 128-wide row, and the
helper raised:

    CB rope: group 1 hidden_dim (128) not a multiple of per-head width
             (256; fused=True)

The raise lands inside `cb_retrieve_pre_computed`'s handler, so the server
answers `scatter_ran=False` instead of hanging and the client degrades the
request TP-collectively. Measured on an 8-way H200 M3 run: every CB retrieve
failed this way (408 degrades = 8 ranks x 51 calls) with `blend_loads` 0, so
the blend never engaged. Output stayed correct because each request fell back
to a full recompute, which is why this presented as a silent 0.0 blend rate
rather than a crash.

Let the group's own declared per-head width (`shape_desc.hs`, i.e. what vLLM
allocated) decide whether the format's fused claim applies to it. Both signals
are required, so this can only narrow a fused claim: a format that is not
fused stays not fused, and a group carrying no `shape_desc` keeps the
format-only decision.

The index group then resolves to `(fused=False, per_head=128, n_heads=1)` and
is rotated as one K plane, which is correct: M3's write kernel ropes index-K at
the token's absolute position, so those keys must be re-RoPE'd when a token is
reused at a different position. Skipping the group instead would leave stale
positions in the indexer and silently perturb its top-k block selection.

Verified against the installed 0.5.5.dev63 build: the new
`test_mixed_registration_key_only_group_is_not_fused` fails before the change
and passes after, with the file's 19 pre-existing cases green both ways.

commits.author: Divy
commits.message:
[Bugfix][MP] Complete async copies before their buffers are reused (#4830)

* fix(mp): complete async copies before their buffers are reused

Two places in the engine-driven path launch async copies and then hand the
buffers to something that reads them, without waiting. Both fail silently:
the KV is already committed or already scattered, so the only symptom is
corrupted content much later. Found while running the engine-driven pickle
transport on 8xH100, where it showed up as a gsm8k score dropping from 0.80
to 0.00 with no error anywhere.

scatter_cpu_to_paged_kv pins unpinned chunks into temporaries and launches
async H2D reads on them through raw pointers, which torch's stream tracking
cannot see. Returning drops the last reference, so the caching host
allocator can hand that memory to the next caller while the copies are
still in flight and the next pin_memory() overwrites the bytes mid-transfer.
The caller-side synchronize the function documents cannot cover this: by
then the temporaries are already gone. Sync before returning, but only when
we pinned them -- caller-owned pinned chunks keep the existing fast path.

submit_store synchronized only when out_buffers was given, i.e. the SHM
path. Gather issues async device->CPU copies on both transports, and the
pickle transport serializes the buffers immediately in commit_store, so the
pickle path was serializing a buffer still being written. Make it
unconditional.

Both tests run without a GPU so they hold in the CPU-only unit CI, and both
fail without the corresponding fix. The pickle one asserts a sync falls
between gather and commit rather than merely occurring: submit_store also
syncs before prepare_store, and that earlier call is why guarding the second
on out_buffers went unnoticed.

Signed-off-by: Divy <divy@coralbricks.ai>

* test(mp): satisfy mypy in the async-copy lifetime tests

commit_store's side effect used `order.append(...) or True`, and append
returns None, so mypy rejected it as func-returns-value. Replaced with a
typed function. The scatter test passes MagicMock chunks on purpose
(pin_memory needs an accelerator, so the ptr-only branch cannot execute on
the CPU-only CI), so the call now casts them explicitly.

Signed-off-by: Divy <divy@coralbricks.ai>

  toolchain needs.

  asm in ld_cs/st_cs behind `!defined(USE_MACA)` instead of removing it,
  so real CUDA builds keep the optimization and MACA builds fall through
  to the portable path.
- requirements/maca_core.txt: placeholder, no MACA-specific runtime
  package identified yet.
- docs: add a MetaX MACA tab under "From Source" installation docs.

No CI/wheel publishing is included by design (self-compile only).

Verified on MetaX C500 hardware: BUILD_WITH_MACA=1 python setup.py
build_ext --inplace compiles lmcache.cuda_ops successfully and the
extension imports with all expected native symbols.

commits.author: Samuel Shen
commits.message:
[Refactor]: vLLM LBHNC KVLayout metadata (#4729)

* [Fix] Restore vLLM KV cache layout discovery after vllm#51718

vllm#51718 (RFC vllm#42082) moved layout resolution onto
CacheConfig.kv_cache_layout and removed
vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils.get_kv_cache_layout, so the kv_layout
registration hint silently vanished on vLLM nightlies.

Read the resolved layout from CacheConfig (falling back to the legacy
backend query on older vLLM), normalize standardized KVCacheLayout
names onto the existing NHD/HND vocabulary, and raise at registration
for the four layouts LMCache cannot transfer yet instead of
misclassifying them as NHD.

Part of #3560.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Clarify unsupported-layout remediation: backend-required layouts cannot be overridden via env

Found in E2E: DeepSeek V4's attention backend requires BLHNC, so the
previous suggestion to set VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT was not actionable there
(backend-required outranks the env var in vLLM's resolution order).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* [Fix] Express LMCache's preferred KV cache layout to vLLM

Non-MLA models prefer the standardized head-contiguous layout (LBHNC);
MLA defers since layout is immaterial for a single latent head, and
pre-standardization vLLM gets the legacy HND name. The standardized
name is returned rather than its alias because MultiConnector compares
preference strings verbatim. Backend-required layouts and
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT still outrank a preference and remain validated
at registration.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Keep LayoutHints.kv_layout strictly NHD/HND; translate at the vLLM boundary

Review feedback: kv_layout exists only to disambiguate the heads/tokens
order that shape sniffing cannot; engine formats live in EngineKVFormat.
Move the standardized-name translation (and the unsupported-layout
fail-loud) from kv_format/types.py into integration/vllm/utils.py, and
have the detector reject hints outside the two-value contract instead
of importing a vLLM vocabulary.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Fail loud when layout hints are built before resolution

Registration always runs after vLLM resolves the layout, so an
unresolved CacheConfig here means a caller bug (hints built at
construction time, or an ambient default config); raise with the
precondition instead of silently skipping the hint. The MP worker
adapter captures hints once per process -- the layout is final for the
process lifetime and heartbeat recovery may re-register from a context
without the ambient vLLM config.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Support the blocks-first standardized layouts (BLHNC/BLNHC)

The kv_layout hint now carries the standardized layout vocabulary
(legacy NHD/HND spellings canonicalize at the vLLM boundary), and the
vLLM detector goes declaration-first: a blocks-first hint makes it
verify that the registered per-layer views share one storage with the
declared strides -- any drift raises -- and reconstruct the single
cross-layer tensor.

Two EngineKVFormat members join their NB_NL_TWO_* siblings with K/V
packed in the content dim: NB_NL_NH_BS_CS (BLHNC) and NB_NL_BS_NH_CS
(BLNHC). Their specs hand the kernels per-layer base pointers one
(layer, block) chunk apart, and page_buffer_offset gains the inflated
per-block step (num_layers * chunk) that blocks-first addressing
needs. GPU round-trip tests pin the kernels against a pure-torch
reference in both directions.

LHBNC and BHLNC remain rejected: their per-(layer, block) content is
fragmented per head, which PageBufferShapeDesc cannot describe.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Blocks-first transfers through HMA-shared pools

DeepSeek V4's pool interleaves groups with different geometry, so a
group's per-block step exceeds num_layers * chunk. Reconstruction now
accepts (and preserves) the observed step, the connector reads it off
the reconstructed tensor, and multi_layer_kv_transfer carries it to
the kernels as block_stride_elems (0 = tight). Pointer initialization
goes through spec.data_ptrs so cross-layer formats hand the kernels
per-layer bases. GPU round-trip tests cover tight and padded pools.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Reconstruct blocks-first groups interleaved inside HMA blocks

DeepSeek V4 pools weave groups within each block, so one group's
consecutive layers sit a uniform step apart that exceeds its own
chunk. Observe and verify the step (uniform spacing, block step large
enough to hold all layers), carry it as the reconstructed tensor's
layer stride, and let the per-layer base pointers absorb it in the
kernels.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Carry canonical layout names and reconstructed tensors through the MP group path

Found by MP-mode E2E: the subpaged-MLA group edit still enforced the
legacy two-name kv_layout contract and rejected canonical names, and
per-group discovery integer-indexed the reconstructed cross-layer
tensor as if it were a per-layer list. Group edits now accept the
canonical spellings, and cross-layer sub-groups keep their single
reconstructed tensor (identity grouping folds the repeats).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Identity grouping reads geometry off the reconstructed cross-layer tensor

Cross-layer entries in the normalized per-layer list are the whole
reconstructed tensor, not per-layer slices; indexing the outer list by
layer fed a list into the spec accessors.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Group representatives resolve their spec source through one helper

Third occurrence of the same slip (engine discovery, identity grouping,
now the layer-groups manager): a cross-layer group's representative
entry is the reconstructed whole-group tensor and must not be wrapped
as a per-layer list. group_spec_source() owns the choice.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Route every group-representative spec access through group_spec_source

The layer-groups manager's block-stride probe and shape-desc builder
still passed the outer per-layer list for cross-layer groups.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Group data pointers resolve cross-layer groups locally

get_group_data_ptrs passed the outer per-layer list and global layer
indices; a cross-layer group's spec needs its reconstructed tensor and
group-local indices. Adds a DSV4-shaped construction test: two groups
with different geometry interleaved in one blocks-first pool, through
normalize -> manager -> group pointers.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* MP block-transfer kernels address the blocks-first formats

Per-layer base pointers land one (layer, block) chunk apart and
scalars_per_block() already carries the interleaved step through
block_stride_elems, so the new formats reuse the per-layer address
shape; NB_NL_NH_BS_CS joins the HND within-block branch.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Apply isort and clang-format across the branch

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Import the MP connector lazily in the preference tests

Importing lmcache_mp_connector at collection time initializes
process-wide MP transfer state, which the cache-server tests later
trip over when the whole suite runs in one process. The isolation
defect predates this branch; importing inside a fixture keeps the
preference tests out of that ordering.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Note why the heads-outermost layouts stay unsupported

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Mark the heads-outermost layout gap as TODO

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Treat layout hints as registration payload, not adapter-computed state

The connector already builds the hints for group edits; forward them
through register_kv_caches and persist them beside kv_caches and
engine_group_infos for heartbeat re-registration, instead of the
adapter lazily computing its own copy from the ambient config.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Scope the CPU-backend HND override to layer-compact hints

The override works around vLLM's CPU attention backend misreporting
the layer-compact layout; it was also stomping explicit blocks-first
declarations, which broke reconstruction everywhere torch runs on CPU
(the ubuntu CI matrix).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Match the torch fallback's multi_layer_kv_transfer signature to cuda_ops

The CUDA binding gained block_stride_elems; the fallback mirrors it
and rejects the blocks-first cross-layer formats it does not
implement, following the file's existing HND precedent. Caught by
test_function_signature_parity on k3.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Resolve cross-layer entries inside the spec accessors

Review feedback: the geometry accessors own the mapping from a
normalized per-layer structure onto what a format's spec expects, so
call sites stay uniform. One documented resolver replaces the
per-call-site source juggling and the group_spec_source helper, and
bare cross-layer tensors pass through unchanged again.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Own the kv_layout vocabulary in kv_format.types

The canonical-spelling map was declared in the vLLM detector and
re-spelled inline in the group edits; the vocabulary module that
defines KVLayoutName owns it now and both consume it.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Skip the connector preference tests where vLLM is not installed

The k3 unit environment installs LMCache without vLLM; the lazy
connector import now skips there instead of erroring.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Split the data_ptrs docstring into one paragraph per pointer shape

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Resolve block_stride_elems through the layout getter

Both connector classes computed it inline from is_cross_layer checks;
route them through resolve_block_stride_and_log_layout and give the
torch fallback an _is_blocks_first_format predicate beside its
existing _is_*_format helpers.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Trim comments to load-bearing facts

Also fix the NB_NL_BS_NH_CS module docstring (the [BS, NH, CS] order
is NHD, not HND) and move the enum doc comments for 17/18 in front of
their members like the rest of the file.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop layout-name canonicalization; keep NHD and HND

translate_vllm_kv_cache_layout now maps vLLM's LBNHC/LBHNC to NHD/HND
at the boundary, so hints and detection keep the names LMCache has
always used, plus BLHNC/BLNHC which have no legacy spelling. Deletes
CANONICAL_KV_LAYOUTS. get_required_kvcache_layout still returns
LBHNC because that string goes to vLLM.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Leave kv_cache_group_edits.py untouched

With hints carrying NHD/HND again the file needs no change; restore
it to dev byte for byte.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop drive-by edits to unrelated files

Restore two READMEs, the cache-simulator README, and
record_strategies/base.py, which a repo-wide format pass had
reformatted; none are touched by this change. Keep the dev wording of
the kv_layout hint doc, appending only the new names.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Keep get_num_blocks at two arguments

The cross-layer unwrap lives inside the getter, so dev's call site
works unchanged for every group and kv_layer_groups.py returns to dev
byte for byte.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Name the fallback guard for what it tests

Blocks-outermost is not the same as cross-layer: TRT-LLM's
NB_NL_TWO_NH_BS_HS is cross-layer without fused KV and the NL_X_*_CS
formats are fused without being cross-layer; the fallback supports
both. The guard rejects exactly the cross-layer fused pair, so call
it that.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Derive every layout-name check from KVLayoutName

KVLayoutName is the one place the accepted vocabulary is written;
KV_LAYOUT_NAMES = get_args(KVLayoutName) feeds the membership checks
and the return annotations use the type. Deletes the
_UNSUPPORTED/_KNOWN tuple globals from the vLLM integration.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Return only the spec input from _resolve_spec_view

Cross-layer spec accessors ignore per-call layer indices, so the
resolved local index was never load-bearing; callers keep passing
their own.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Spell out shapes in the reconstruction docstring

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop the blocks-first reconstruction; read the block step from stride(0)

vLLM's per-layer views under BLHNC/BLNHC have exactly the shape of the
existing NL_X_NB_NH_BS_CS / NL_X_NB_BS_NH_CS formats -- only stride(0)
differs, and contiguous-view recovery already accepts dim-0-padded
views. So detection classifies them as those formats with the views
passed through, the two per-layer CS offset entries take the block
step from block_stride_elems (0 means tight, as before), and
resolve_block_stride_and_log_layout treats the CS formats as
block-axis. Deletes NB_NL_NH_BS_CS / NB_NL_BS_NH_CS, their specs, the
reconstruction, and _resolve_spec_view.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Tile the mamba state row without assuming divisibility

Nightly vLLM registers the aligned mamba state as a tight view: the
page padding lives only in stride(0), so the row no longer divides by
the unified block size. Round the per-token width up to the widest
vector alignment that tiles within the block step and divides it; the
spilled columns land in the page padding and stride(0) stays the
dim-0 step. Verified MP E2E on Kimi Linear and Qwen3-Next.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Bound the mamba tile by the layer's padded page, not stride(0)

On a shared pool stride(0) spans sibling layers, so a rounded-up tile
could cover the next layer's bytes and a stale load would corrupt it.
spec.page_size_bytes is this layer's own allotment; spill stays inside
it.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Move get_size_bytes to lmcache.utils

It is engine-agnostic and the core (memory management, allocators)
imported it from the vLLM integration module, inverting the layering
and creating an import cycle through lmcache.v1.gpu_connector. The
old name re-exports; the cycle-dodging function-level import of
KV_LAYOUT_NAMES becomes a plain module import.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Rely on vLLM's own layout parsing

CacheConfig.get_resolved_kv_cache_layout() owns alias resolution,
unknown-name validation, and the not-yet-resolved error, so the
translation shrinks to the member-name -> LMCache-name map plus the
heads-outermost rejection.

commits.message:
[Platform][RBLN] Add RBLN device backend for engine-driven MP transfer (#4450)

* [Platform][RBLN] Add RBLN device backend for engine-driven MP transfer

Adds Rebellions NPUs as a device-registry entry. `torch.rbln` comes from
torch-rbln through a torch backend entry point, so it is visible on a bare
`import torch`; the engine is vllm-rbln. Without a registry entry,
detection falls back to the CPU stub and no RBLN path works at all.

Scope is multiprocess engine-driven transfer, which is self-contained: the
MP path builds no GPU connector, resolving layouts through
`normalize_kv_and_discover_format` and moving KV through `RblnDeviceOps`.
The in-process connector follows separately.

LMCache-driven MP is refused up front. `torch.rbln` exposes device
discovery, `set_device()` and `synchronize()` but no `Stream` / `Event`,
and that path orders its cross-process handoff with an event, so
`RblnDeviceSpec` reports `is_handle_transfer_available()` as False and
leaves `ipc_wrapper_cls` / `event_ipc_backend` at their None defaults --
`mp_transfer_mode=lmcache_driven` then fails at its documented validation
point instead of on an attribute lookup later.

The per-layer KV cache is 6-D: vllm-rbln allocates
`[2, NB, NH, 1, BS, HS]`, HND with an extra axis between heads and block
tokens that the RBLN attention backend requires. Axis 3 is always 1, so the
bytes and strides are those of NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_BS_HS one axis short.

It is registered as its own EngineKVFormat.NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS (15)
rather than squeezed into format 6 during discovery. Reshaping inside
detection would need a device hook, making discovery depend on
process-global device state instead of being a pure function of
`(kv_caches, layout_hints)`, and would force a second device-specific rule
for a layout that is HND by definition. As its own format, the 6-D branch
in `detectors/vllm.py` keys off the shape signature alone (rank 6, leading
axis 2, axis 3 == 1), so the same input classifies identically on any host,
the detector needs no `rbln` entry in its HND table, and the reported
layout -- which vllm-rbln never sets, leaving `get_kv_cache_layout()` at
its NHD default -- plays no part.

Squeezing the axis in `attempt_permute_to_contiguous_view` was also
rejected: a blanket singleton squeeze silently misclassifies vLLM HND with
`num_kv_heads == 1` (any TP size equal to the KV-head count) as a rank-4
blocks-first fused format, and breaks SGLang MLA outright, whose detection
keys off `shape[1] == 1`.

No transfer kernel handles format 15. RBLN has no compiled block-transfer
extension in tree, and the CUDA / SYCL kernels never see an RBLN cache, so
their `default:` arm rejecting it is correct rather than a gap. csrc
carries only the enum value and its `FORMAT_FACTS` row; `ops_types.py`
mirrors the value, which `test_c_ops_parity` requires to match exactly.

`RblnDeviceOps` inherits the torch baseline for every op except
`multi_layer_block_kv_transfer`, which stages each chunk head-major
(`[2, L, H, T, D]`) rather than upstream's token-major `[2, L, T, H*D]`.
Filling a token-major chunk from an HND paged buffer costs an on-device
head/token permute per store and restore; head-major issues none. The
chunk keeps the byte size upstream sized it to and is reinterpreted with a
free view. Sound because the engine-driven pair writes and reads it with
the same code and the cache server treats it as an opaque byte range. It
applies `squeeze_singleton_axis` at entry, so `kv_ops.py` indexes a 5-D
tensor and the singleton stays out of every axis offset below.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Platform][RBLN] Drop the unused is_native_kv_structure predicate

The predicate was the tolerant guard for a `normalize_kv_caches` hook on
`DeviceSpec`: format discovery handed the hook every KV structure it saw,
so the RBLN override had to recognize a flat list of native 6-D tensors
and pass everything else through untouched.

That design is gone. The native layout is now its own
`EngineKVFormat.NL_X_TWO_NB_NH_ONE_BS_HS`, detection reshapes nothing,
and the squeeze moved down into `RblnDeviceOps`, which knows from the
detected format what it holds and uses the strict
`squeeze_singleton_axis`. Nothing under `lmcache/` calls the predicate
any more -- only its own test did -- so remove it along with the
`DiscoverableKVCache` import it needed and the design-doc mention.

`is_rbln_kv_layout` stays: `squeeze_singleton_axis` is built on it.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Platform][RBLN] Stage chunks in the canonical token-major wire layout

RblnDeviceOps staged each chunk head-major ([2, L, H, T, D]) to avoid the
head<->token transpose that filling a token-major chunk from an HND cache
requires. That made an RBLN chunk unreadable by any other device, which
is the whole point of a wire layout, and it is not necessary: the
transpose can run on the host instead of inside the device<->host copy.

Chunks are now staged in LMCache's canonical [2, L, T, H*D]. Gather reads
each block's K and V straight out of the paged cache into a host buffer
laid out [B, L, 2, H, BS, D] -- both sides contiguous, no device-side
gather and no device buffer -- and transposes into the chunk on the host.
Scatter mirrors it. K and V are addressed separately because
layer[:, block] spans both halves of a layer and is not contiguous.

Measured on Qwen3-1.7B (28L, 8 heads, head_size 128, bf16, block 1024,
one block per chunk):

  gather  D2H   19.5 GB/s   (head-major staging reached 3.8 GB/s here)
  scatter H2D   19.2 GB/s   (head-major staging reached 24.5 GB/s)

so the canonical layout costs nothing on the store path and stays within
reach on the restore path. Block ids being scattered rather than
contiguous makes no difference: no copy spans a block boundary either
way.

test_chunk_matches_the_canonical_torch_path pins the output byte-for-byte
against the shared torch path. The staging buffers are thread-local: the
multiprocess server runs blocking handlers on a thread pool, so a store
and a retrieve can be in multi_layer_block_kv_transfer at once, and
sharing one buffer corrupted the KV cache with no error raised.
test_staging_concurrency covers that and fails on a shared buffer.

Signed-off-by: rebel-jinhwan <jinhwan.suk@rebellions.ai>

commits.author: Hoang Minh An
commits.message:
fix(mp): don't let one bad frame kill the shared client polling loop (#4765)

* fix(mp): don't let one bad frame kill the shared client polling loop

`ClientPollingLoop` runs a single process-wide daemon thread that services
every `MessageQueueClient`, and `_main_loop` calls `owner.process_inbound()`
without a guard. `process_inbound` decodes peer-supplied bytes in four places,
so any decode failure propagates out of the loop and terminates the thread.
Nothing supervises or restarts it, so every client in the process is stranded:
pending futures never resolve and new requests only ever time out, until the
process is restarted. The traceback goes to the dying thread's stderr, so
nothing actionable surfaces to the application.

This is reachable today between adjacent releases. `RequestType` is an
`enum.auto()` enum, so a member's wire value is its declaration position, and
the list is not append-only: between v0.5.2 (36 members) and v0.5.4 (40) three
members were inserted at positions 3-5, shifting 34 existing values (STORE 3->6,
RETRIEVE 4->7, PING 19->22) and extending the range. A peer on the newer
protocol therefore answers with values an older peer cannot decode. Since the
cache-server and engine-side images are versioned independently, a mismatched
pair is an ordinary deployment state.

Wrap the dispatch so an undecodable or otherwise unexpected frame is logged and
dropped while the loop keeps serving. The offending request still times out --
without a usable request_type it cannot be matched to its future -- but the
blast radius is now that one request instead of the whole process.

The regression test asserts the observable contract through the public API
only: after a response the client cannot decode, a later well-formed request
must still complete. Without the guard that second request times out too.

Signed-off-by: anhm5 <anhm5@fpt.com>

* fix(mp): annotate the futures in the new polling-loop test for mypy

The new test carries a `-> None` annotation, so unlike its neighbours mypy
checks its body. `submit_request` returns `MessagingFuture[T]` and the call
does not pass `response_cls`, leaving `T` unbound, so mypy asks for an explicit
annotation on both locals. `GET_CHUNK_SIZE` responds with `int`.

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Fix][CB] Decide fused-KV packing per group, not per registration (#4850)

`_cb_group_rope_geometry` read `is_fused_packed` from the group's
`engine_kv_format`, but that format is detected once per REGISTRATION while
fused-ness is a per-GROUP property.

MiniMax-M3 registers a fused `2 * head_size` main K/V group (60 layers)
alongside a key-only `head_size` lightning-indexer side cache (57 layers).
Both are rank 4 -- the fused signature -- and both report `kv_size == 1`, so
the shared format labelled the index group fused too. `per_head` became
`2 * head_size`, which does not divide that group's 128-wide row, and the
helper raised:

    CB rope: group 1 hidden_dim (128) not a multiple of per-head width
             (256; fused=True)

The raise lands inside `cb_retrieve_pre_computed`'s handler, so the server
answers `scatter_ran=False` instead of hanging and the client degrades the
request TP-collectively. Measured on an 8-way H200 M3 run: every CB retrieve
failed this way (408 degrades = 8 ranks x 51 calls) with `blend_loads` 0, so
the blend never engaged. Output stayed correct because each request fell back
to a full recompute, which is why this presented as a silent 0.0 blend rate
rather than a crash.

Let the group's own declared per-head width (`shape_desc.hs`, i.e. what vLLM
allocated) decide whether the format's fused claim applies to it. Both signals
are required, so this can only narrow a fused claim: a format that is not
fused stays not fused, and a group carrying no `shape_desc` keeps the
format-only decision.

The index group then resolves to `(fused=False, per_head=128, n_heads=1)` and
is rotated as one K plane, which is correct: M3's write kernel ropes index-K at
the token's absolute position, so those keys must be re-RoPE'd when a token is
reused at a different position. Skipping the group instead would leave stale
positions in the indexer and silently perturb its top-k block selection.

Verified against the installed 0.5.5.dev63 build: the new
`test_mixed_registration_key_only_group_is_not_fused` fails before the change
and passes after, with the file's 19 pre-existing cases green both ways.

Signed-off-by: deng451e <838677410@qq.com>

commits.author: Divy
commits.message:
[Bugfix][MP] Complete async copies before their buffers are reused (#4830)

* fix(mp): complete async copies before their buffers are reused

Two places in the engine-driven path launch async copies and then hand the
buffers to something that reads them, without waiting. Both fail silently:
the KV is already committed or already scattered, so the only symptom is
corrupted content much later. Found while running the engine-driven pickle
transport on 8xH100, where it showed up as a gsm8k score dropping from 0.80
to 0.00 with no error anywhere.

scatter_cpu_to_paged_kv pins unpinned chunks into temporaries and launches
async H2D reads on them through raw pointers, which torch's stream tracking
cannot see. Returning drops the last reference, so the caching host
allocator can hand that memory to the next caller while the copies are
still in flight and the next pin_memory() overwrites the bytes mid-transfer.
The caller-side synchronize the function documents cannot cover this: by
then the temporaries are already gone. Sync before returning, but only when
we pinned them -- caller-owned pinned chunks keep the existing fast path.

submit_store synchronized only when out_buffers was given, i.e. the SHM
path. Gather issues async device->CPU copies on both transports, and the
pickle transport serializes the buffers immediately in commit_store, so the
pickle path was serializing a buffer still being written. Make it
unconditional.

Both tests run without a GPU so they hold in the CPU-only unit CI, and both
fail without the corresponding fix. The pickle one asserts a sync falls
between gather and commit rather than merely occurring: submit_store also
syncs before prepare_store, and that earlier call is why guarding the second
on out_buffers went unnoticed.

Signed-off-by: Divy <divy@coralbricks.ai>

* test(mp): satisfy mypy in the async-copy lifetime tests

commit_store's side effect used `order.append(...) or True`, and append
returns None, so mypy rejected it as func-returns-value. Replaced with a
typed function. The scatter test passes MagicMock chunks on purpose
(pin_memory needs an accelerator, so the ptr-only branch cannot execute on
the CPU-only CI), so the call now casts them explicitly.

commits.author: weishu
commits.message:
[Fix][CB] Decide fused-KV packing per group, not per registration (#4850)

`_cb_group_rope_geometry` read `is_fused_packed` from the group's
`engine_kv_format`, but that format is detected once per REGISTRATION while
fused-ness is a per-GROUP property.

MiniMax-M3 registers a fused `2 * head_size` main K/V group (60 layers)
alongside a key-only `head_size` lightning-indexer side cache (57 layers).
Both are rank 4 -- the fused signature -- and both report `kv_size == 1`, so
the shared format labelled the index group fused too. `per_head` became
`2 * head_size`, which does not divide that group's 128-wide row, and the
helper raised:

    CB rope: group 1 hidden_dim (128) not a multiple of per-head width
             (256; fused=True)

The raise lands inside `cb_retrieve_pre_computed`'s handler, so the server
answers `scatter_ran=False` instead of hanging and the client degrades the
request TP-collectively. Measured on an 8-way H200 M3 run: every CB retrieve
failed this way (408 degrades = 8 ranks x 51 calls) with `blend_loads` 0, so
the blend never engaged. Output stayed correct because each request fell back
to a full recompute, which is why this presented as a silent 0.0 blend rate
rather than a crash.

Let the group's own declared per-head width (`shape_desc.hs`, i.e. what vLLM
allocated) decide whether the format's fused claim applies to it. Both signals
are required, so this can only narrow a fused claim: a format that is not
fused stays not fused, and a group carrying no `shape_desc` keeps the
format-only decision.

The index group then resolves to `(fused=False, per_head=128, n_heads=1)` and
is rotated as one K plane, which is correct: M3's write kernel ropes index-K at
the token's absolute position, so those keys must be re-RoPE'd when a token is
reused at a different position. Skipping the group instead would leave stale
positions in the indexer and silently perturb its top-k block selection.

Verified against the installed 0.5.5.dev63 build: the new
`test_mixed_registration_key_only_group_is_not_fused` fails before the change
and passes after, with the file's 19 pre-existing cases green both ways.

Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

The single_layer_kv_transfer / single_layer_kv_transfer_sgl C++ functions
take a non-const torch::Tensor& slot_mapping. The refactor wrapped them in
lambdas that declared slot_mapping as const torch::Tensor&, causing a
'discards qualifiers' compile error. Restore non-const binding.

* fix(c_ops): accept int for lmcache_memcpy_async direction instead of the enum
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

TransferDirection/EngineKVFormat are owned by the lmache_native module only,
so c_ops must not export them. lmcache_memcpy_async was still bound via a raw
function pointer whose 4th param is the C++ TransferDirection type, requiring
a TransferDirection object from the same module. Wrap it in a lambda that takes
an int and casts to TransferDirection, matching the other c_ops bindings and
letting callers pass the enum value (implicitly converted to int).

* refactor: rename storage_manager csrc dir and namespace to lmcache_native

lmcache::storage_manager C++ namespace to lmcache::lmcache_native
to match the existing pybind module name (lmache_native). Update

* fix: avoid duplicate pybind11 enum registration in xpu_ops
Signed-off-by: baoloongmao <307499405@qq.com>

with plain int direction/engine_kv_format args plus static_cast, matching

commits.author: Samuel Shen
commits.message:
[Refactor]: vLLM LBHNC KVLayout metadata (#4729)

* [Fix] Restore vLLM KV cache layout discovery after vllm#51718

vllm#51718 (RFC vllm#42082) moved layout resolution onto
CacheConfig.kv_cache_layout and removed
vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils.get_kv_cache_layout, so the kv_layout
registration hint silently vanished on vLLM nightlies.

Read the resolved layout from CacheConfig (falling back to the legacy
backend query on older vLLM), normalize standardized KVCacheLayout
names onto the existing NHD/HND vocabulary, and raise at registration
for the four layouts LMCache cannot transfer yet instead of
misclassifying them as NHD.

Part of #3560.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Clarify unsupported-layout remediation: backend-required layouts cannot be overridden via env

Found in E2E: DeepSeek V4's attention backend requires BLHNC, so the
previous suggestion to set VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT was not actionable there
(backend-required outranks the env var in vLLM's resolution order).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* [Fix] Express LMCache's preferred KV cache layout to vLLM

Non-MLA models prefer the standardized head-contiguous layout (LBHNC);
MLA defers since layout is immaterial for a single latent head, and
pre-standardization vLLM gets the legacy HND name. The standardized
name is returned rather than its alias because MultiConnector compares
preference strings verbatim. Backend-required layouts and
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT still outrank a preference and remain validated
at registration.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Keep LayoutHints.kv_layout strictly NHD/HND; translate at the vLLM boundary

Review feedback: kv_layout exists only to disambiguate the heads/tokens
order that shape sniffing cannot; engine formats live in EngineKVFormat.
Move the standardized-name translation (and the unsupported-layout
fail-loud) from kv_format/types.py into integration/vllm/utils.py, and
have the detector reject hints outside the two-value contract instead
of importing a vLLM vocabulary.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Fail loud when layout hints are built before resolution

Registration always runs after vLLM resolves the layout, so an
unresolved CacheConfig here means a caller bug (hints built at
construction time, or an ambient default config); raise with the
precondition instead of silently skipping the hint. The MP worker
adapter captures hints once per process -- the layout is final for the
process lifetime and heartbeat recovery may re-register from a context
without the ambient vLLM config.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Support the blocks-first standardized layouts (BLHNC/BLNHC)

The kv_layout hint now carries the standardized layout vocabulary
(legacy NHD/HND spellings canonicalize at the vLLM boundary), and the
vLLM detector goes declaration-first: a blocks-first hint makes it
verify that the registered per-layer views share one storage with the
declared strides -- any drift raises -- and reconstruct the single
cross-layer tensor.

Two EngineKVFormat members join their NB_NL_TWO_* siblings with K/V
packed in the content dim: NB_NL_NH_BS_CS (BLHNC) and NB_NL_BS_NH_CS
(BLNHC). Their specs hand the kernels per-layer base pointers one
(layer, block) chunk apart, and page_buffer_offset gains the inflated
per-block step (num_layers * chunk) that blocks-first addressing
needs. GPU round-trip tests pin the kernels against a pure-torch
reference in both directions.

LHBNC and BHLNC remain rejected: their per-(layer, block) content is
fragmented per head, which PageBufferShapeDesc cannot describe.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Blocks-first transfers through HMA-shared pools

DeepSeek V4's pool interleaves groups with different geometry, so a
group's per-block step exceeds num_layers * chunk. Reconstruction now
accepts (and preserves) the observed step, the connector reads it off
the reconstructed tensor, and multi_layer_kv_transfer carries it to
the kernels as block_stride_elems (0 = tight). Pointer initialization
goes through spec.data_ptrs so cross-layer formats hand the kernels
per-layer bases. GPU round-trip tests cover tight and padded pools.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Reconstruct blocks-first groups interleaved inside HMA blocks

DeepSeek V4 pools weave groups within each block, so one group's
consecutive layers sit a uniform step apart that exceeds its own
chunk. Observe and verify the step (uniform spacing, block step large
enough to hold all layers), carry it as the reconstructed tensor's
layer stride, and let the per-layer base pointers absorb it in the
kernels.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Carry canonical layout names and reconstructed tensors through the MP group path

Found by MP-mode E2E: the subpaged-MLA group edit still enforced the
legacy two-name kv_layout contract and rejected canonical names, and
per-group discovery integer-indexed the reconstructed cross-layer
tensor as if it were a per-layer list. Group edits now accept the
canonical spellings, and cross-layer sub-groups keep their single
reconstructed tensor (identity grouping folds the repeats).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Identity grouping reads geometry off the reconstructed cross-layer tensor

Cross-layer entries in the normalized per-layer list are the whole
reconstructed tensor, not per-layer slices; indexing the outer list by
layer fed a list into the spec accessors.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Group representatives resolve their spec source through one helper

Third occurrence of the same slip (engine discovery, identity grouping,
now the layer-groups manager): a cross-layer group's representative
entry is the reconstructed whole-group tensor and must not be wrapped
as a per-layer list. group_spec_source() owns the choice.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Route every group-representative spec access through group_spec_source

The layer-groups manager's block-stride probe and shape-desc builder
still passed the outer per-layer list for cross-layer groups.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Group data pointers resolve cross-layer groups locally

get_group_data_ptrs passed the outer per-layer list and global layer
indices; a cross-layer group's spec needs its reconstructed tensor and
group-local indices. Adds a DSV4-shaped construction test: two groups
with different geometry interleaved in one blocks-first pool, through
normalize -> manager -> group pointers.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* MP block-transfer kernels address the blocks-first formats

Per-layer base pointers land one (layer, block) chunk apart and
scalars_per_block() already carries the interleaved step through
block_stride_elems, so the new formats reuse the per-layer address
shape; NB_NL_NH_BS_CS joins the HND within-block branch.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Apply isort and clang-format across the branch

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Import the MP connector lazily in the preference tests

Importing lmcache_mp_connector at collection time initializes
process-wide MP transfer state, which the cache-server tests later
trip over when the whole suite runs in one process. The isolation
defect predates this branch; importing inside a fixture keeps the
preference tests out of that ordering.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Note why the heads-outermost layouts stay unsupported

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Mark the heads-outermost layout gap as TODO

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Treat layout hints as registration payload, not adapter-computed state

The connector already builds the hints for group edits; forward them
through register_kv_caches and persist them beside kv_caches and
engine_group_infos for heartbeat re-registration, instead of the
adapter lazily computing its own copy from the ambient config.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Scope the CPU-backend HND override to layer-compact hints

The override works around vLLM's CPU attention backend misreporting
the layer-compact layout; it was also stomping explicit blocks-first
declarations, which broke reconstruction everywhere torch runs on CPU
(the ubuntu CI matrix).

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Match the torch fallback's multi_layer_kv_transfer signature to cuda_ops

The CUDA binding gained block_stride_elems; the fallback mirrors it
and rejects the blocks-first cross-layer formats it does not
implement, following the file's existing HND precedent. Caught by
test_function_signature_parity on k3.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Resolve cross-layer entries inside the spec accessors

Review feedback: the geometry accessors own the mapping from a
normalized per-layer structure onto what a format's spec expects, so
call sites stay uniform. One documented resolver replaces the
per-call-site source juggling and the group_spec_source helper, and
bare cross-layer tensors pass through unchanged again.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Own the kv_layout vocabulary in kv_format.types

The canonical-spelling map was declared in the vLLM detector and
re-spelled inline in the group edits; the vocabulary module that
defines KVLayoutName owns it now and both consume it.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Skip the connector preference tests where vLLM is not installed

The k3 unit environment installs LMCache without vLLM; the lazy
connector import now skips there instead of erroring.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Split the data_ptrs docstring into one paragraph per pointer shape

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Resolve block_stride_elems through the layout getter

Both connector classes computed it inline from is_cross_layer checks;
route them through resolve_block_stride_and_log_layout and give the
torch fallback an _is_blocks_first_format predicate beside its
existing _is_*_format helpers.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Trim comments to load-bearing facts

Also fix the NB_NL_BS_NH_CS module docstring (the [BS, NH, CS] order
is NHD, not HND) and move the enum doc comments for 17/18 in front of
their members like the rest of the file.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop layout-name canonicalization; keep NHD and HND

translate_vllm_kv_cache_layout now maps vLLM's LBNHC/LBHNC to NHD/HND
at the boundary, so hints and detection keep the names LMCache has
always used, plus BLHNC/BLNHC which have no legacy spelling. Deletes
CANONICAL_KV_LAYOUTS. get_required_kvcache_layout still returns
LBHNC because that string goes to vLLM.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Leave kv_cache_group_edits.py untouched

With hints carrying NHD/HND again the file needs no change; restore
it to dev byte for byte.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop drive-by edits to unrelated files

Restore two READMEs, the cache-simulator README, and
record_strategies/base.py, which a repo-wide format pass had
reformatted; none are touched by this change. Keep the dev wording of
the kv_layout hint doc, appending only the new names.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Keep get_num_blocks at two arguments

The cross-layer unwrap lives inside the getter, so dev's call site
works unchanged for every group and kv_layer_groups.py returns to dev
byte for byte.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Name the fallback guard for what it tests

Blocks-outermost is not the same as cross-layer: TRT-LLM's
NB_NL_TWO_NH_BS_HS is cross-layer without fused KV and the NL_X_*_CS
formats are fused without being cross-layer; the fallback supports
both. The guard rejects exactly the cross-layer fused pair, so call
it that.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Derive every layout-name check from KVLayoutName

KVLayoutName is the one place the accepted vocabulary is written;
KV_LAYOUT_NAMES = get_args(KVLayoutName) feeds the membership checks
and the return annotations use the type. Deletes the
_UNSUPPORTED/_KNOWN tuple globals from the vLLM integration.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Return only the spec input from _resolve_spec_view

Cross-layer spec accessors ignore per-call layer indices, so the
resolved local index was never load-bearing; callers keep passing
their own.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Spell out shapes in the reconstruction docstring

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Drop the blocks-first reconstruction; read the block step from stride(0)

vLLM's per-layer views under BLHNC/BLNHC have exactly the shape of the
existing NL_X_NB_NH_BS_CS / NL_X_NB_BS_NH_CS formats -- only stride(0)
differs, and contiguous-view recovery already accepts dim-0-padded
views. So detection classifies them as those formats with the views
passed through, the two per-layer CS offset entries take the block
step from block_stride_elems (0 means tight, as before), and
resolve_block_stride_and_log_layout treats the CS formats as
block-axis. Deletes NB_NL_NH_BS_CS / NB_NL_BS_NH_CS, their specs, the
reconstruction, and _resolve_spec_view.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Tile the mamba state row without assuming divisibility

Nightly vLLM registers the aligned mamba state as a tight view: the
page padding lives only in stride(0), so the row no longer divides by
the unified block size. Round the per-token width up to the widest
vector alignment that tiles within the block step and divides it; the
spilled columns land in the page padding and stride(0) stays the
dim-0 step. Verified MP E2E on Kimi Linear and Qwen3-Next.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Bound the mamba tile by the layer's padded page, not stride(0)

On a shared pool stride(0) spans sibling layers, so a rounded-up tile
could cover the next layer's bytes and a stale load would corrupt it.
spec.page_size_bytes is this layer's own allotment; spill stays inside
it.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Move get_size_bytes to lmcache.utils

It is engine-agnostic and the core (memory management, allocators)
imported it from the vLLM integration module, inverting the layering
and creating an import cycle through lmcache.v1.gpu_connector. The
old name re-exports; the cycle-dodging function-level import of
KV_LAYOUT_NAMES becomes a plain module import.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Rely on vLLM's own layout parsing

CacheConfig.get_resolved_kv_cache_layout() owns alias resolution,
unknown-name validation, and the not-yet-resolved error, so the
translation shrinks to the member-name -> LMCache-name map plus the
heads-outermost rejection.

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

* Document the mamba re-view by input and output shape and stride

Signed-off-by: Samuel Shen <slshen@tensormesh.ai>

commits.message:
[Fix][RawBlock] Cap uring_cmd auto transfer size by max_segments (#3882)

[Bugfix] raw_block: cap auto max_data_transfer_size by NVMe max_segments

With use_uring_cmd=true, _resolve_max_data_transfer_size auto-detected the I/O split size from max_hw_sectors_kb only, ignoring the device's max_segments scatter-gather limit. The NVMe io_uring_cmd passthrough builds one iovec segment per page, so a transfer larger than max_segments*page_size is rejected by the kernel with EINVAL and every large store/load fails.

Cap the auto-detected size at min(max_hw_sectors_kb*1024, max_segments*page_size), falling back to the max_hw_sectors_kb value when max_segments sysfs is absent.

[MP][Ascend] Ascend NPU multiprocess format support + generic engine-driven path (#3968)

* [MP][Ascend] support Ascend NPU and the per-layer (K, V) tuple KV format

Add Ascend NPU as a first-class platform and introduce the per-layer
(K, V) tuple engine KV format (NL_X_TWO_X_NB_BS_NH_HS) produced by
vLLM-Ascend, where layers are outermost and each layer carries its own
(K, V) pair of paged [num_blocks, block_size, num_heads, head_size]
tensors.

Platform:
- New NpuDeviceInfo detection entry (lmcache/v1/platform/npu) that loads
  the lmcache_ascend.c_ops backend on an NPU host; native kernels stay
  in the LMCache-Ascend plugin.
- New Ascend build profile (setup_extensions/build_profiles/ascend.py):
  detects the CANN toolchain via ASCEND_HOME_PATH and supplies the ABI
  flags; the upstream package builds only the common C++ extensions.

KV format (NL_X_TWO_X_NB_BS_NH_HS):
- Register the enum value across the C++ header, pybind bindings, and the
  Python fallback, and add the orthogonal is_kv_second_tuple modifier.
- Allow tuples in DiscoverableKVCache, list-depth probing, and device
  lookup so the native per-layer (K, V) structure is recognized end to
  end; add a vLLM detector branch and a format spec.
- Add the _transfer_per_layer_kv_tuple path, which transposes the
  structure to the SGLang MHA [[K_layers], [V_layers]] layout the kernel
  consumes.
- Route the transfer context gather/scatter through get_device /
  get_dtype / get_group_data_ptrs instead of tensors[0], so the nested
  per-layer tuple layout resolves device, dtype, and plane pointers
  correctly.

Tests:
- Extend the format-classification golden tests to pin the new format's
  structural partition and the is_kv_second_tuple modifier.
- Add compute_kv_layout and accessor/grouping tests for the tuple format.

[Fix][RawBlock] Bounce unaligned buffers in io_uring uring_cmd read paths (#3891)

Multi-page NVMe passthrough builds a PRP list whose entries must each be
page-aligned. read_uring only enforced this under use_odirect, and
batched_read had no bounce path at all, so unaligned buffers under
use_uring_cmd hit EINVAL on transfers larger than one page.

mirror its bounce logic in batched_read. Add 4 env-guarded tests verifying
unaligned read/batched_read, short-buffer bounce, and per-item decisions.
Verified on Samsung PM1753.
